item.title: “Monks, evil, unwholesome states arise with a sign, not without a sign. By abandoning that sign, those evil, unwholesome states are not present. Monks, evil,…
item.description:
“Monks, evil, unwholesome states arise with a sign, not without a sign. By abandoning that sign, those evil, unwholesome states are not present. Monks, evil, unwholesome states arise with a cause, not without a cause. By abandoning that cause, those evil, unwholesome states are not present. Monks, evil, unwholesome states arise with a form, not without a form … arise with a feeling … with a perception … with consciousness, not without consciousness. By abandoning that cause, those evil, unwholesome states are not present.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 2.77

item.title: "The monk, secluding himself from sensual desires, secluding himself from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial and…
item.description:
"The monk, secluding himself from sensual desires, secluding himself from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. He drenches, saturates, fills, and pervades his very body with the rapture and pleasure born of seclusion, so that no spot on his entire body is not pervaded by that rapture and pleasure born of seclusion."

From: Dīgha Nikāya 2 – Sāmaññaphalasutta

item.title: “Monks, a man, attending to his own male faculties, male deportment, male attire, male nature, male desires, male voice, male adornment — becomes lustful and…
item.description:
“Monks, a man, attending to his own male faculties, male deportment, male attire, male nature, male desires, male voice, male adornment — becomes lustful and delights in them. Through being lustful and delighting in them, he attends to external female faculties, female deportment, female attire, female nature, female desires, female voice, female adornment, and becomes lustful and delights in them. Through being lustful and delighting in them, he desires external bonding. With that bonding as condition, pleasure and joy arise, and he desires that pleasure and joy. Monks, through delighting in their own masculinity, beings become bonded to women. Thus, monks, a man does not escape his own masculinity.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.51

item.title: Elder Uttara: “Nothing exists here that is permanent, No conditioned thing is everlasting. The aggregates arise and cease, They pass away in another existence. Knowing…
item.description:
Elder Uttara:
“Nothing exists here that is permanent,
No conditioned thing is everlasting.
The aggregates arise and cease,
They pass away in another existence.

Knowing this danger,
I do not desire existence.
Having abandoned all sensual desires,
I have realized the destruction of defilements.”

From: Theragāthā 2.1
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “And craving, previously unknowing — which is of sensual desire, of defilement — that state is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a…
item.description:
“And craving, previously unknowing — which is of sensual desire, of defilement — that state is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, unable to arise again in the future. And anger, previously unknowing — which is of ill-will, of fault — that state is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, unable to arise again in the future. And ignorance, previously unknowing — which is of delusion, of fault — that state is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, unable to arise again in the future. Therefore, a monk thus attained has attained the supreme peace of the peaceful state. Monks, this is the supreme noble peace — namely, the peace of greed, hatred, and delusion.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 140 – Dhātuvibhaṅgasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, how is a monk a samana (ascetic)? He has quieted down evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful…
item.description:
“Monks, how is a monk a samana (ascetic)? He has quieted down evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful results, leading to future birth, aging, and death. Thus, monks, a monk is a samana.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 39 – Mahāhatthipadopamasutta

item.title: “Bound with sinews and bones, Plastered with flesh and skin, This body is covered by skin — Truth is not seen as it is. Within,…
item.description:
“Bound with sinews and bones,
Plastered with flesh and skin,
This body is covered by skin —
Truth is not seen as it is.

Within, it is full of liver, bladder,
Heart, lungs,
Kidneys and spleen,
Nasal mucus, saliva, sweat, fat,
Blood, synovial fluid, bile, and lymph.

From these nine streams,
Impurity constantly flows —
From the eyes, discharge flows,
From the ears, discharge flows.

From the nostrils, mucus flows,
From the mouth, sometimes vomit —
Bile and phlegm flow —
From the body, sweat and dirt.

In the hollow of the head,
The brain is full.
The fool, led by ignorance,
Thinks it is beautiful.

When it lies dead, swollen,
Livid, discarded in a charnel ground,
Relatives no longer care.

Dogs, jackals, wolves, worms,
Crows, vultures, and other creatures eat it.”

From: Sutta Nipāta 1.11
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “He who dwells attending to the beautiful, Unrestrained in the senses, Immoderate in food, Lazy, inactive — Māra overthrows him As wind a weak tree.”…
item.description:
“He who dwells attending to the beautiful,
Unrestrained in the senses,
Immoderate in food,
Lazy, inactive —
Māra overthrows him
As wind a weak tree.”

“He who dwells contemplating the foul,
Well-restrained in the senses,
Moderate in food,
Faithful, energetic —
Māra does not overthrow him,
As wind a rocky mountain.”

From: Dhammapada 1-20

item.title: Elder Nun Sumedhā: Remember this human body — Compared to a water bubble — Full of misfortunes, Empty, without core — See the aggregates as…
item.description:
Elder Nun Sumedhā:

Remember this human body —
Compared to a water bubble —
Full of misfortunes,
Empty, without core —
See the aggregates as impermanent!
Remember the many dangers of hell.

Remember the great charnel ground —
Because of continuous rebirth —
Because of fear of crocodiles —
Remember the Four Noble Truths.

The deathless water is here —
Why would one drink a hundred bitters?
All sensual pleasures
Are truly a hundred thousand bitter.

The deathless water is here!
Why would one delight in feverish sensual pleasures?
All sensual pleasures burn,
Seething and blistering.

There are no enemies here!
Why delight in hostile sensual pleasures?
The king of fire, thieves, water, enemies —
Common enemies are many.

Here there is liberation!
Why let sensual pleasures kill and bind?
In sensual pleasures there is killing and binding —
Delighting in sensual pleasures brings much suffering.

A blazing grass torch —
If you hold it and don’t let go, you’ll be burned.
Sensual pleasures are like a torch —
They burn anyone who doesn’t escape.

Do not accept small sensual pleasures,
Abandoning great, expansive happiness.
Do not be like a fish swallowing a hook,
Then later suffering calamity.

Subdue sensual desire within sensual desires,
Like a dog tied with a leash.
Do not let sensual desires devour you,
Like a hungry man devouring a dog.

Suffering is truly boundless,
It causes much mental distress.
You are tied to sensual desires —
Abandon impermanent sensual desires.

Here, there is no aging!
Why pursue sensual desires that age?
Every birth, everywhere,
Is subject to disease and death —

Here there is no aging, no death —
This is the path without aging,
Without death, without sorrow,
Without enemies, without bonds,
Without stumbling, without fear,
Without burning, without falling.

This goal, many have attained —
This goal is the deathless.
Now it should be realized.
If one is rightly attentive,
Without exertion,
One cannot realize it.

This is the cause, the source —
This is the very root —
Endure the Teacher’s word!
This is the first link —
That is Nibbāna —
If we love the Dhamma.

Thus, with faith,
They spoke these excellent words,
Words full of wisdom —
Supreme, ultimate —
They are disgusted with renewed existence —
Through disgust, craving ceases.

From: Therīgāthā 16.1
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “That is so, great king. That is so, great king. All beings are subject to death, end in death, and do not escape death. Just…
item.description:
“That is so, great king. That is so, great king. All beings are subject to death, end in death, and do not escape death. Just as, great king, all the pots made by a potter, whether unfired or fired, are subject to breakage, end in breakage, and do not escape breakage — so too, great king, all beings are subject to death, end in death, and do not escape death.

All beings will die,
Life ends with death,
According to their kamma they go,
Reaping fruits of good and evil —
Evil kamma leads to hell,
Good kamma to heaven.
Therefore do good,
Accumulate for the future life,
Merits for the future life
Are a support for beings.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 3.22
